narrativeReportMd:
# RiskEvidenceSynthesis R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
RiskEvidenceSynthesis is a hard breaking removal for R6 consumers: R4 instances with resourceType RiskEvidenceSynthesis have no same-identity R6 StructureDefinition to validate against. The R6 package marks the name as an old type, and the likely replacement pattern is the broader Evidence resource rather than a renamed one-to-one resource.

## Scope
The local R4 StructureDefinition was compared with the R6 package index, R6 old-types CodeSystem, and R6 Evidence/EvidenceVariable definitions as likely migration context. Base Resource/DomainResource changes and separate SearchParameter artifacts are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration is not a field-preserving version bump. Implementers must change the resource type to Evidence, remodel population/exposure/outcome references into role-classified variableDefinition entries, move risk estimates and sample size into statistic structures, and review certainty and terminology semantics.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the absence of a same-name R6 resource. The next highest risks are conversion and code-generation breaks caused by the remodel of required top-level PICO references and riskEstimate/sampleSize into Evidence.variableDefinition and Evidence.statistic.

## Findings requiring human review
Element-level mapping confidence is medium because no official ConceptMap or narrative migration guide was found in the local inputs. Human review is especially important for denominator/numerator mapping, confidence-interval level normalization, and certainty-rating semantics.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 Evidence model appears more general and expressive, but the removal of the old concrete resource identity is inherently disruptive. A deprecated alias, explicit cross-version extension set, or computable ConceptMap would have reduced migration ambiguity.

## Follow-up analysis
A full report for Evidence and EvidenceVariable, plus terminology expansion review for statistic/certainty/synthesis value sets, should be used before automating production migrations.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: RiskEvidenceSynthesis is absent as an R6 resource, so R4 instances are not valid R6 instances by resource identity. The most important migration concerns are the resource-type replacement by Evidence, the remodel of population/exposure/outcome into variableDefinition roles, and the remodel of riskEstimate/sampleSize/certainty into richer statistic and certainty structures. Confidence is high for the removal itself and medium for detailed field mappings because no official ConceptMap was found locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat migration as a resource transformation rather than a simple schema update. Preserve canonical identifiers where possible, change resourceType to Evidence only with explicit mapping rules, represent population/exposure/outcome through Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole plus observed/intended references, represent risk estimates through Evidence.statistic.quantity and related count/sampleSize elements, and normalize certainty/precision terminology with review.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: The identity finding is high confidence because the direct R6 file is absent, the R6 index has no RiskEvidenceSynthesis StructureDefinition entry, and the R6 old-types CodeSystem lists the name. Element-level migration findings are medium confidence because they are inferred from the likely R6 Evidence model and local element definitions, not from an official migration map or narrative diff.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. A conformant R6 validator or generated R6 model set has no RiskEvidenceSynthesis resource definition, so an R4 instance with resourceType RiskEvidenceSynthesis cannot be accepted as an R6 instance by preserving the same resource type. Runtime risk is critical for parsers, code generators, switch statements, repositories, search indexes, subscriptions, and APIs that key behavior on resourceType.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Systems exchanging evidence syntheses could silently drop, reject, or misclassify clinical evidence summaries if the resource-type migration is not explicit.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate evidence-synthesis concepts into the broader Evidence resource model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A less-breaking base design could have retained RiskEvidenceSynthesis as a deprecated compatibility resource or formal alias while directing new content to Evidence.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal of consolidating risk-evidence synthesis into the broader Evidence model is reasonable, and the local R6 package supports that RiskEvidenceSynthesis is no longer a current resource. A less-breaking base design was possible, but preserving the old resource identity would materially undercut consolidation by leaving two base resource representations for substantially overlapping evidence-synthesis content. That makes the break probably justified, though it remains high-impact and should have been paired with explicit migration guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest base-design alternative would have been to keep `RiskEvidenceSynthesis` in R6 as a deprecated compatibility resource, possibly tightly constrained to map to `Evidence`, while making `Evidence` the preferred model. That would preserve most R4-valid instances at the resourceType level. The tradeoff is not just conversion work: it would create ongoing duplicate resource identities, duplicate generated classes/endpoints/search behavior, and interoperability pressure to support both forms indefinitely. A ConceptMap or conversion tool alone would be useful mitigation but is not counted as a backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve legacy instances but keep duplicate resource identities and legacy endpoints/search/model surface in the base specification.

findings.narrativeMd: RiskEvidenceSynthesis itself is removed from the R6 resource set. This is the most important breaking change because it occurs before any element-level comparison: the resourceType token that makes an R4 instance a RiskEvidenceSynthesis is no longer recognized as a current R6 resource. Any implementation that generated a RiskEvidenceSynthesis class, endpoint, validator, search compartment, or persistence table must choose an explicit migration target rather than relying on version-tolerant parsing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid RiskEvidenceSynthesis instance can become R6-invalid solely because the root resource type has no R6 StructureDefinition. Conversely, an R6 Evidence instance that represents risk evidence cannot be represented in R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis by changing only resourceType; the variable, statistic, and certainty structures must be transformed and may contain R6-only content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory every use of resourceType RiskEvidenceSynthesis in data, APIs, generated models, validators, subscriptions, search indexes, and business rules. Define an explicit transform to Evidence or to a local compatibility profile/extension strategy, preserve canonical url/identifier/version fields where meaningful, and keep regression tests for old instances that contain population, exposure, outcome, riskEstimate, sampleSize, and certainty.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader Evidence model may be a sound long-term design, but deleting or renaming a resource type is not backward compatible. A compatibility alias, deprecated wrapper, or official ConceptMap would have lowered migration risk while still allowing new R6 systems to prefer Evidence.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official ballot narrative or change logs before final migration design. The local package proves absence from R6 core, but not the committee rationale or complete intended mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines RiskEvidenceSynthesis as a concrete resource, while the R6 package has no RiskEvidenceSynthesis StructureDefinition and marks the name as an old FHIR type. That is a real resource identity break: an R4 instance with resourceType RiskEvidenceSynthesis is not a same-shape R6 instance, and generated models, resource-type dispatch, endpoints, repositories, and search handling keyed to the old type need an explicit migration. However, this was an FMM 0 trial-use resource, public evidence for routine production exchange is limited, and R6 Evidence appears to be the broader replacement model for the same evidence-variable, statistic, and certainty concepts. Preserving the old resource identity in base R6 would reduce migration pain but would also leave duplicate resource identities for overlapping content.

That is a plausible but materially costly partial alternative rather than a clearly better base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing report: it correctly identifies a hard resource identity break and a possible compatibility-resource alternative, but the Critical impact overstates the action concern once FMM 0 and the lack of quick production-use evidence are considered.

findings.title: Population, exposure, and outcome references are remodeled as Evidence.variableDefinition roles

oldState.summary: R4 uses named top-level references: population 1..1, exposure 0..1, and outcome 1..1, all targeting EvidenceVariable.
oldState.narrativeMd: RiskEvidenceSynthesis required population and outcome as distinct top-level fields and allowed one optional exposure field. Their names carried the PICO role directly.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence uses repeatable variableDefinition entries with required variableRole codes and observed/intended references to Group or EvidenceVariable.
newState.narrativeMd: Evidence.variableDefinition is repeatable, classifies each variable by a required variableRole code, and separates observed from intended variable definitions. It can also reference Group and represent covariates, which have no direct R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis top-level counterpart.

facts.newValue: Evidence.variableDefinition[*] with variableRole=population; no base minimum requiring a population entry
Evidence.variableDefinition[*] with variableRole=outcome; no base minimum requiring an outcome entry

facts.oldValue: population, optional exposure, outcome as separate fields
facts.newValue: variableRole required binding includes population, exposure, outcome, and covariate

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match is based on equivalent research-question roles and R6 Evidence comments saying comparative evidence is often defined with population, exposure, and outcome variables.

impact.impactRationaleMd: If Evidence is used as the R6 migration target, the old top-level fields are not accepted at their old paths. Generated R4 code that expects .population, .exposure, and .outcome cannot read the R6 structure without role-based selection logic. R6 content can contain multiple variables, covariates, intended versus observed references, and Group targets that are not cleanly representable in the three R4 fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapping a population, exposure, comparator, covariate, or outcome changes the clinical interpretation of an evidence statement.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent comparative and non-comparative evidence variables uniformly and allow richer roles and observed/intended distinctions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have kept deprecated named population/exposure/outcome fields alongside role-based variableDefinition entries during a transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A unified `variableDefinition` model with explicit roles, Group/EvidenceVariable targets, covariates, and observed-versus-intended distinctions is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking alias approach would preserve common R4 patterns, but it would be incomplete for richer R6 cases and would introduce validation ambiguity when both old named fields and role-based entries are present. Those material tradeoffs support a `Probably justified` verdict rather than treating the break as clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternative would have been to retain deprecated `population`, `exposure`, and `outcome` elements, or a deprecated compatibility wrapper carrying them, while adding `variableDefinition` as the normalized R6 representation. That would cover straightforward R4 instances with one population, optional exposure, and one outcome. It would not fully cover multiple variables, covariates, Group targets, or observed/intended distinctions, and it would require invariants or precedence rules to prevent divergent duplicate encodings. A published mapping would reduce migration burden but would be mitigation rather than a base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases would ease common R4 migrations but create duplicate ways to encode the same variables and require consistency rules.

evidence.detail: R4 population is 1..1 Reference(EvidenceVariable).
R4 outcome is 1..1 Reference(EvidenceVariable).
R6 Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole is 1..1 code with required binding to variable-role.
R6 observed references Group or EvidenceVariable.
R6 intended references Group or EvidenceVariable and distinguishes intended variable from actual observed variable.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows a simple role-preserving mapping. It does not decide whether R4 references should become observed or intended; that distinction needs domain-specific review.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 encoded the research-question roles as three named fields, with population and outcome mandatory. R6 Evidence makes variables a repeatable backbone and uses a required role code to express population, exposure, outcome, or covariate. This remodel is more flexible but breaks code that assumes direct properties and creates a real semantic choice between observed and intended references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 elements at population, exposure, and outcome are not valid paths in R6 Evidence. R6 Evidence can also express cases that R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis cannot represent directly, including multiple variables of the same role, covariates, Group references, and observed/intended distinctions. Missing population or outcome may be R6-valid at the base level but would be unrepresentable as a valid R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis without invented references.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define role-based mapping rules. For simple R4 instances, create one variableDefinition for each existing population, exposure, and outcome reference, set variableRole accordingly, and choose intended or observed based on migration policy. Add tests for missing optional exposure, multiple R6 variables, Group targets, and covariates that need extensions or cannot round-trip.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably motivated by a more general evidence model. It could have been made less disruptive by keeping deprecated alias elements or providing a standard ConceptMap and invariants linking aliases to variableDefinition entries.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The observed-versus-intended choice is not derivable from the old field name alone. Human review or a project-level policy is needed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The old model used named top-level population, exposure, and outcome references, with population and outcome required. The R6 Evidence model instead uses repeatable variableDefinition entries classified by a required variableRole code and separates observed from intended variable definitions, with Group added as a possible reference target. This breaks old generated access patterns and makes R6-to-R4 conversion lossy for covariates, multiple variables, Group references, or cases where observed and intended differ. Still, the R6 design goal is coherent: it generalizes evidence variables beyond the fixed PICO slots and makes roles explicit. Keeping the old named fields alongside variableDefinition would help simple migrations but would create duplicate encodings and consistency rules.
keyEvidence: R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.population is 1..1 Reference(EvidenceVariable); exposure is 0..1 Reference(EvidenceVariable); outcome is 1..1 Reference(EvidenceVariable).
R6 Evidence.variableDefinition is 0..* and Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole is 1..1 code with required variable-role binding including population, exposure, outcome, and covariate.
R6 Evidence.variableDefinition.observed and intended each reference Group or EvidenceVariable.
R4 maturity map: RiskEvidenceSynthesis is FMM 0, trial-use.
Targeted web search did not find prominent documented production exchange of RiskEvidenceSynthesis.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens the compatibility burden, but these paths are central to the artifact's evidence interpretation, so I still considered the concrete mapping and safety consequences rather than dismissing the break outright.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old code expecting direct .population, .exposure, and .outcome properties must switch to role-based selection; R6-to-R4 loss is also possible for richer variableDefinition cases.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained deprecated population, exposure, and outcome fields or a compatibility wrapper while adding variableDefinition. That would preserve common R4 instances, but it would be incomplete for covariates, multiple variables, Group targets, and observed-versus-intended distinctions, and it would require precedence or invariants when both representations appear.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and partial alternative analysis: the mapping risk is real and clinically meaningful, but low FMM and the material tradeoffs of retaining duplicate fields make the remodel probably acceptable.

findings.title: riskEstimate and sampleSize are remodeled into Evidence.statistic

oldState.summary: R4 has one optional riskEstimate and one optional top-level sampleSize.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 riskEstimate contains description, type, decimal value, unitOfMeasure CodeableConcept with required UCUM binding, denominatorCount, numeratorCount, and repeatable precisionEstimate with level/from/to decimal values. sampleSize is a separate top-level backbone with description, numberOfStudies, and numberOfParticipants.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence has repeatable statistic entries with quantity, counts, nested sampleSize, and nested attributeEstimate.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Evidence.statistic is 0..* and contains statisticType, quantity, numberOfEvents, numberAffected, nested sampleSize with unsignedInt counts, and attributeEstimate for confidence intervals and other attributes. R6 defines attributeEstimate.level as 0.95 for a 95% confidence interval, whereas the R4 precisionEstimate.level definition says to use 95.

facts.newValue: statistic.numberAffected unsignedInt, depending on statistic semantics

facts.oldValue: riskEstimate.denominatorCount integer and top-level sampleSize.numberOfParticipants integer
precisionEstimate.from/to decimal and level where 95 means 95% CI
facts.newValue: attributeEstimate.range Range and level where 0.95 means 95% CI

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match is based on R6 Evidence.statistic definitions for statistic value, number affected/events, sample size, and attribute estimates corresponding to R4 riskEstimate, numerator/denominator counts, sampleSize, and precisionEstimate.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data at riskEstimate and sampleSize cannot be read by R6 Evidence code without a structural transform. The transform is not purely mechanical for denominatorCount, numeratorCount, units, and confidence interval level because the R6 model uses Quantity, multiple statistic entries, more count fields, and different documented scaling for confidence level.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect mapping of numerator, denominator, unit, or confidence interval can change the quantitative meaning of risk evidence.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize risk estimates into a reusable statistic model that can represent many statistic types and attributes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have retained deprecated riskEstimate/sampleSize elements while adding the generalized Evidence.statistic model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The generalized `Evidence.statistic` structure is a reasonable R6 design goal because it supports multiple statistics, richer count distinctions, nested sample size, and attribute estimates. Keeping the old `riskEstimate` and top-level `sampleSize` shape would reduce migration breakage for common R4 instances, but the duplicate quantitative model would create persistent ambiguity over numerator, denominator, unit, interval level, and which representation is authoritative. Those tradeoffs are material, so the breaking remodel is probably justified even though explicit conversion guidance remains important.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have added `Evidence.statistic` while keeping deprecated `riskEstimate` and `sampleSize` fields, either on a retained compatibility resource or as aliases with strict invariants. This would preserve simple R4 data but would not naturally represent multiple statistics or the richer R6 count and attribute-estimate model. Duplicate same-fact fields could diverge and would likely accumulate long-term compatibility burden. A normative ConceptMap would help implementers but, by itself, would be migration tooling rather than a backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve many old quantitative fragments but leave duplicate statistical representations and difficult consistency semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 riskEstimate.value is 0..1 decimal.
R4 unitOfMeasure is 0..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to UCUM units.
R4 precisionEstimate.level is decimal and the definition says to use 95 for a 95% confidence interval.
R6 statistic.quantity is 0..1 Quantity for the statistic value.
R6 sampleSize is nested under statistic and includes numberOfStudies, numberOfParticipants, knownDataCount, and numberAnalyzed as unsignedInt fields.
R6 attributeEstimate.level definition says to use 0.95 for a 95% confidence interval.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates a plausible transform for a proportion with a confidence interval. It intentionally shows the 95 to 0.95 level normalization that should be tested.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis used a purpose-built riskEstimate backbone. R6 Evidence uses a generic statistic backbone that can support more than risk and can repeat. This affects both JSON shape and clinical/statistical meaning: numerator and denominator are not simply renamed, the unit moves from a CodeableConcept to a Quantity representation, and precision estimates become attribute estimates with Range or Quantity values.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances carrying riskEstimate or top-level sampleSize cannot be treated as R6 Evidence without moving data. R6 Evidence can contain multiple statistics, model characteristics, nested attribute estimates, and count distinctions that R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis cannot round-trip. Some R4 integer values that are negative would be invalid if mapped to R6 unsignedInt fields, although negative counts would generally be nonsensical data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build explicit conversion tests for riskEstimate.value/unitOfMeasure, numeratorCount, denominatorCount, sampleSize, and precisionEstimate. Normalize confidence levels from 95 to 0.95 where appropriate, map interval bounds to Range.low/high, and require review where denominatorCount could mean total participants, known data count, or analyzed count. Preserve unmapped details with extensions only with documented semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The statistic remodel is probably justified by the broader Evidence resource, but the old dedicated field names could have been retained temporarily or accompanied by a normative mapping. Without that, migration logic must be locally defined and validated with domain examples.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Do not automate denominator/numerator mapping solely by field name. The correct R6 target depends on statistic type and analysis context.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had one optional riskEstimate backbone and one optional top-level sampleSize backbone. R6 Evidence uses repeatable statistic entries with Quantity values, nested sampleSize counts, and repeatable attributeEstimate entries for intervals and related statistical attributes. This is not a simple rename: generated APIs change, confidence interval level changes from 95-style to 0.95-style documentation, and numerator, denominator, participant, known-data, and analyzed counts can require context-sensitive mapping. Even so, the generalized statistic model is a reasonable R6 direction for an immature evidence-synthesis resource because it supports multiple statistics and richer quantitative metadata. Retaining the R4 quantitative structure would preserve simple cases but create duplicate and potentially divergent statistical representations.
keyEvidence: R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.riskEstimate is 0..1 with value decimal, unitOfMeasure CodeableConcept required to UCUM, denominatorCount, numeratorCount, and precisionEstimate.
R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.sampleSize is 0..1 with numberOfStudies and numberOfParticipants integer fields.
R6 Evidence.statistic is 0..* with statistic.quantity Quantity, statistic.sampleSize, and statistic.attributeEstimate.
R4 precisionEstimate.level definition says use 95 for a 95% interval; R6 attributeEstimate.level says use 0.95.
R4 maturity map: RiskEvidenceSynthesis is FMM 0, trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The FMM 0 trial-use status reduces the expectation that R6 must preserve this exact quantitative shape. I still treated the path as important because incorrect numeric mapping can change the meaning of evidence.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: old riskEstimate and sampleSize accessors do not map mechanically to the R6 statistic model; R6-to-R4 loss can occur for multiple statistics and richer count or attribute distinctions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept deprecated riskEstimate and sampleSize fields while adding Evidence.statistic. The tradeoff is substantial: duplicate fields would need consistency rules, the old shape cannot naturally express multiple statistics or richer R6 count semantics, and consumers would need to decide which representation is authoritative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and partial alternative reasoning: the remodel creates real migration risk, but the generalized statistic model has enough justification and the compatibility alternative has enough cost that the break is probably OK.

findings.title: Certainty representation changes cardinality, terminology, and nesting semantics

oldState.summary: R4 certainty has repeatable rating and repeatable certaintySubcomponent with type, repeatable rating, and notes.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 certainty.rating is 0..* CodeableConcept bound extensibly to evidence-quality. certaintySubcomponent is a child backbone with type, repeatable rating, and note.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence.certainty has type, single rating, rater, and recursive subcomponent.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Evidence.certainty.rating is 0..1 CodeableConcept with an example binding, certainty.type identifies the aspect being rated, rater can identify who rated it, and certainty.subcomponent recursively references Evidence.certainty.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 elements have the same broad purpose, but their internal structure and terminology changed enough that a one-to-one field rename is unsafe.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The resource removal is the primary validation break, but certainty also has its own migration risk. R4 certainty entries with multiple ratings in one certainty do not map to R6 single-rating entries without splitting or choosing one. R6 recursive subcomponents and rater attribution have no direct R4 fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Certainty ratings affect interpretation of evidence quality and decision support trust.

justification.inferredGoal: Model certainty as rated aspects with recursive subcomponents and optional attribution.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have kept certainty.rating repeatable while adding certainty.type, rater, and recursive subcomponents.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of richer certainty modeling is reasonable, but the specific cardinality break from repeatable ratings to a single rating per certainty entry does not appear necessary from the local evidence. Allowing `rating` to remain `0..*` while recommending one rating per typed certainty aspect would preserve R4 certainty content and still support the new type/rater/subcomponent structure. Because that alternative has relatively moderate tradeoffs, this part of the remodel looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base alternative would have retained `Evidence.certainty.rating` as `0..*` and added clearer definitions or best-practice guidance that separate certainty aspects should usually be represented as separate typed certainty entries. This would preserve old multi-rating certainty fragments and still allow recursive subcomponents and rater attribution. The tradeoff is that validators could not enforce the normalized single-rating pattern in the base model, so consumers would still need to handle multiple ratings on one certainty entry; that is a manageable compatibility cost compared with forcing data splitting.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost would be weaker normalization of one rating per certainty aspect, not duplicate fields or loss of the richer model.

evidence.detail: R4 certainty.rating is 0..* CodeableConcept with extensible evidence-quality binding.
R4 certaintySubcomponent is repeatable and has type, rating, and note children.
R6 Evidence.certainty.rating is 0..1 CodeableConcept with example certainty-rating binding.
R6 Evidence.certainty.subcomponent is recursive via contentReference #Evidence.certainty.

examples.examplesMd: The example focuses on the certainty fragment and omits required R4 root fields. It illustrates that multiple old ratings may need splitting into multiple R6 certainty entries or a policy decision.

findings.narrativeMd: Certainty did not merely move from one resource to another. The R6 model changes how a rating is associated with an aspect of certainty and uses recursion for subcomponents. Old implementations that expected an array of ratings on a certainty object need to decide whether each rating becomes a separate R6 certainty, a subcomponent, or a retained extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An old certainty fragment is not valid at the old path in R6 Evidence, and even after moving it, multiple ratings in a single old certainty cannot be represented in one R6 certainty.rating because the new cardinality is 0..1. R6 certainty.rater and recursively nested subcomponents are not directly representable in R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Split multi-rating certainty entries when the ratings represent different certainty aspects. Map old certaintySubcomponent.type to R6 certainty.subcomponent.type where possible, map ratings through terminology review, and preserve ambiguous notes or alternate frameworks with extensions or reviewer annotations. Test multi-rating and nested-subcomponent cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The recursive certainty model may be justified for richer evidence grading, but allowing repeated rating during a transition or publishing a mapping profile would have reduced data-loss risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology review is needed because the old evidence-quality and certainty-subcomponent value sets are not the same as R6 certainty-type/certainty-rating bindings.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 certainty allowed multiple ratings on a certainty entry and multiple ratings on each certaintySubcomponent. R6 Evidence.certainty keeps repeatable certainty entries and recursive subcomponents, but each certainty.rating is only 0..1 and the terminology is shifted to example-bound certainty type/rating value sets. The richer R6 model with type, rater, and recursive subcomponents is reasonable, but the local evidence does not show why the rating cardinality needed to narrow. Old content with multiple ratings must be split or collapsed, which can require judgment about whether ratings are alternatives, multiple scales, or separate certainty aspects. A base design that kept rating repeatable while recommending one rating per typed certainty aspect looks comparatively low cost.
keyEvidence: R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.certainty.rating is 0..* CodeableConcept with extensible evidence-quality binding.
R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis.certainty.certaintySubcomponent is 0..* with type and rating, and certaintySubcomponent.rating is 0..*.
R6 Evidence.certainty.rating is 0..1 CodeableConcept with example certainty-rating binding.
R6 Evidence.certainty.subcomponent is recursive through contentReference #Evidence.certainty, and Evidence.certainty.rater is available.
R4 maturity map: RiskEvidenceSynthesis is FMM 0, trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens the general stability claim, but it does not by itself justify an avoidable cardinality narrowing on a semantic field where migration can be lossy or expert-dependent.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6's recursive model has new expressiveness, while R4 multi-rating certainty fragments cannot be represented as a single R6 certainty entry without splitting or dropping ratings.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design exists: keep Evidence.certainty.rating as 0..* and add guidance that normalized content should usually use one rating per typed certainty entry. This preserves old multi-rating content and still supports rater attribution and recursive subcomponents. The main tradeoff is weaker enforcement of normalization, not duplicate fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing alternative judgment that a less-breaking design was available, and the fresh review treats that avoidable cardinality narrowing as enough to merit Revisit despite the existing Medium impact score.

findings.title: Evidence-related terminology bindings changed or weakened in the R6 Evidence model

affectedLocation.newPath: Evidence.synthesisType / studyDesign / statistic.statisticType / attributeEstimate.type / certainty.type / certainty.rating

oldState.summary: R4 uses evidence-synthesis-specific value sets, several with extensible or required binding strength.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 synthesisType and studyType are extensible, riskEstimate.type and precisionEstimate.type are extensible, riskEstimate.unitOfMeasure is required to UCUM units, and certainty.rating is extensible to evidence-quality.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence uses broader statistic/certainty/study-design value sets, often with example binding strength.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Evidence.synthesisType is 0..* with example binding to terminology.hl7.org synthesis-type, studyDesign is extensible to study-design, statisticType is example statistic-type, attributeEstimate.type is example attribute-estimate-type, and certainty type/rating use example bindings.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The value-set comparisons follow the likely structural mapping to Evidence. Terminology expansions were not compared, so code-level equivalence is not asserted.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Weaker example bindings may reduce strict validation failures in R6, but they increase semantic variation and can break generated enums, terminology validation assumptions, analytics groupings, and R6-to-R4 conversion where R4 expected extensible or required bindings. The lack of terminology expansion comparison prevents code-level certainty.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Terminology shifts can alter classification of synthesis method, study design, statistic type, precision type, or certainty rating.

justification.inferredGoal: Move evidence terminology into broader terminology.hl7.org value sets aligned with the generalized Evidence model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is applicable because the reported binding shifts do not by themselves establish an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The terminology changes align with the broader Evidence model and often weaken bindings to `example`, so the local evidence does not show a specific old R4 code becoming invalid in base R6. The main risks are semantic drift, generated-enum assumptions, profile-specific validation, analytics grouping, and R6-to-R4 conversion. Because this finding is not a demonstrated breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue, a backward-compatible alternative judgment is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: If old and new codes are equivalent, including legacy codes in new value sets or publishing ConceptMaps would improve migration safety. If meanings changed, preserving the old codes could reduce semantic clarity. Those steps are important terminology-governance and conversion mitigations, but without evidence of a base R6 validation break they should not be counted as a `Yes` backward-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: ConceptMaps and value-set comparison are still needed for semantic continuity and R6-to-R4 conversion, but they are migration aids rather than base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R4 unitOfMeasure uses a required UCUM units binding.
R4 riskEstimate.type uses an extensible risk-estimate-type binding.
R6 statisticType uses an example statistic-type binding.
R6 certainty.rating uses an example certainty-rating binding.
R6 synthesisType uses an example binding to terminology.hl7.org synthesis-type.

examples.examplesMd: No code-level example is asserted because terminology expansions and ConceptMaps were not available. The risk is in validation/enumeration behavior and semantic grouping, not a specific proven removed code.

findings.narrativeMd: The likely migration target uses different terminology surfaces than R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis. Some bindings move from HL7 FHIR value-set URLs to terminology.hl7.org URLs, some names change from risk/precision-specific to statistic/attribute-specific, and several bindings are weaker in R6. This can be non-breaking for permissive validators but breaking for generated enums, strict profile rules, or analytics keyed to old value-set membership.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A base R6 validator may accept broader terminology where R4 expected extensible or required bindings, but R6 content using new codes may not satisfy R4 profiles or R4 conversion rules. Conversely, R4 codes may need mapping to different R6 value sets to preserve meaning. Without expansions, the exact old-code/new-code compatibility cannot be determined.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not assume old CodeableConcepts are semantically equivalent just because the target element is also CodeableConcept. Compare value-set expansions, add ConceptMaps for synthesis type, study design/type, statistic type, attribute estimate type, certainty type/rating, and test enum/code-system handling in generated clients.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible terminology path would include old codes in new value sets where meanings are unchanged and publish ConceptMaps where names or granularity changed. The tradeoff is carrying legacy terminology and possibly weaker semantic clarity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansion review is required before classifying any individual code as removed, added, or changed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The binding changes are real, but the evidence shown is mostly terminology remodeling and weakening from required or extensible bindings to example bindings in the R6 Evidence model. That does not demonstrate an R4-valid code becoming invalid in base R6. The main concern is semantic continuity, generated enum assumptions, analytics groupings, or R6-to-R4 conversion where new example-bound codes may not fit older value sets. Those are migration and terminology-governance issues, not a strong R4-to-R6 base compatibility break for this low-FMM artifact.
keyEvidence: R4 synthesisType, studyType, riskEstimate.type, precisionEstimate.type, and certainty.rating use extensible bindings; riskEstimate.unitOfMeasure is required to UCUM units.
R6 Evidence.synthesisType, statistic.statisticType, attributeEstimate.type, certainty.type, and certainty.rating use example bindings, while studyDesign is extensible.
R6 Evidence.statistic.quantity is Quantity rather than a separate unitOfMeasure CodeableConcept.
The existing report notes terminology expansions were not compared, so no code-level removal is established.
R4 maturity map: RiskEvidenceSynthesis is FMM 0, trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM further reduces concern where the finding is not a demonstrated old-valid/new-invalid base validation break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: binding and value-set choices changed and may affect terminology assumptions or reverse conversion, but the local evidence does not show a direct R4-to-R6 base validation failure.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed for the reported evidence. Publishing ConceptMaps, including legacy codes where appropriate, or comparing expansions would help migration, but those are terminology governance and mapping aids rather than a necessary base compatibility design change.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact framing for R4-to-R6 compatibility: the report correctly notes no hard instance break and no demonstrated expansion comparison, but those facts support No problem rather than a material break finding.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis snapshot did not show local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints that would require separate migration findings beyond the removed resource and candidate Evidence remodel.

No local slicing or named slices were found in the R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis snapshot. The R6 candidate Evidence mapping uses repeatable backbone elements but not a discovered direct slice correspondence.

No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, regex, fixed, or pattern restrictions were identified in R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis. Numeric datatype shifts such as integer to unsignedInt are covered under the statistic remodel finding rather than as standalone value-limit findings.

R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis includes generic DomainResource constraints and a local naming warning rvs-0. R6 Evidence has comparable canonical/name warnings, but because there is no same-identity R6 artifact, there is no direct local constraint-by-constraint comparison to report apart from the identity and mapping findings.

The old local modifier pattern such as status being marked isModifier is superseded by the resource removal. No separate local modifier-flag-only breaking issue was identified outside the reported resource and element remodels. Inherited modifierExtension behavior is out of scope.

No alternative wire-format change exists for the same RiskEvidenceSynthesis resource because the R6 resource identity is absent. Serialization impact is therefore fully represented by the artifact-identity finding and candidate Evidence structural findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Evidence is active and generalizes evidence variables, statistics, and certainty
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a breaking change within RiskEvidenceSynthesis itself because Evidence is a different R6 resource, not a direct same-identity element change. It is notable because it is the likely migration target.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use the Evidence report and official guidance before treating Evidence as a complete replacement. Its broader scope can represent more than R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis and may require profiling to preserve legacy semantics.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records RiskEvidenceSynthesis as an old FHIR type
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The CodeSystem entry is not itself a validation rule for RiskEvidenceSynthesis instances; the breaking effect comes from the absent R6 StructureDefinition. The marker is useful supporting evidence for removal or rename.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migration tools can use fhir-old-types as a signal that legacy resource names need conversion rather than treating the absence as a packaging accident.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Evidence variable references can target Group as well as EvidenceVariable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Adding Group as a possible target in the likely replacement model is not an R4-to-R6 instance rejection by itself. It is a widening in R6 Evidence.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 conversion must handle Group targets explicitly because R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis population/exposure/outcome targeted only EvidenceVariable.
